I do now publish my Essays; which of all my other works have been most current : for that, as it seems, they come home to men's business and bosoms.

d.t: (UK, soccer) into the goal
d.e:
2004, Tottenham 4-4 Leicester, BBC Sport: February,
Walker was penalised for a picking up a Gerry Taggart backpass and from the resulting free-kick, Keane fired home after Johnnie Jackson's initial effort was blocked.

d.t: (nautical) into the right, proper or stowed position
d.e: sails sheeted home

d.t: To want (something) to happen, with a sense of expectation that it might [with that (+ clause); or (informal) with clause; or with so or (negative) not].
d.e: They are hoping it does not rain, but I expect it will.

d.t: (catenative) To intend to do something and look forward to the prospect of having done it [with to (+ infinitive)].
d.e: I hope to succeed.

d.t: (intransitive) To expect optimistically that one might get something (either a change in circumstance or an object) [with for].
d.e: They're hoping for the best, but I don't think it's looking very good.

d.t: (intransitive) To place confidence; to trust with confident expectation of good [with in].
(transitive, dialectal, nonstandard) To wish.
d.e: I hope you all the best.

d.t: (countable or uncountable) The feeling of trust, confidence, belief or expectation that something wished for can or will happen.
d.e: All hopes for a truce are gone after the latest attack.

d.t: (countable) The actual thing wished for.
(countable) A person or thing that is a source of hope.
d.e: We still have one hope left: my roommate might see the note I left on the table.

d.t: (Christianity, uncountable) The virtuous desire for future good.
(Northern England, Scotland) A hollow; a valley, especially the upper end of a narrow mountain valley when it is nearly encircled by smooth, green slopes; a combe.
A sloping plain between mountain ridges.
(Scotland) A small bay; an inlet; a haven.
A sausage, typically a frankfurter.
d.e: Don't forget to buy some hot dogs to grill and some buns to put them on.

d.t: A food item (dish) consisting of a frankfurter or wiener and (usually) a hot dog bun, with toppings such as ketchup, mustard, relish, sauerkraut, onions, cheese, etc.
d.e: He ordered a hot dog with everything on it.

d.t: A show-off or daredevil, especially in such sports as surfing, skateboarding, or skiing.
(New Zealand) A battered, deep-fried sausage or saveloy on a stick; a corn dog.
(US, education, informal) Describing the shape of a rectangular piece of paper folded in half so that it forms a long rectangle.
(slang, vulgar) The penis.
d.e: I'm just saying, you being a mama, it's time to clear the cobwebs. You know what I'm saying? Put a banana in the monkey. You know, hot dog in your bun.

d.t: (slang, vulgar) A sexually suggestive physical gesture involving movement of the hips.
(slang, intransitive) To perform a dangerous or difficult act or stunt as a display of skill or daring, especially in surfing and other sports.
An expression of delight or enthusiasm.
An expression of disappointment.
(time) A unit of time of one twenty-fourth of a day (sixty minutes).
d.e: Holonyms: day < week < megasecond < fortnight < month < year < gigasecond < century < kiloannum, kiloyear, millennium < terasecond < mega-annum, megayear < petasecond < giga-annum, gigayear < exasecond < zettasecond < yottasecond < ronnasecond < quettasecond

d.t: A season, moment, or time.
d.e: Don't come home ever again at this unearthly hour.

d.t: (poetic) The time.
d.e: The hour grows late and I must go home.

d.t: (military, in the plural) Used after a two-digit hour and a two-digit minute to indicate time.
(chiefly in the plural) The amount of labor demanded by an employer in terms of time.
d.e: I asked my manager for more hours.

d.t: (Christianity, in the plural) The set times of prayer, the canonical hours, the offices or services prescribed for these, or a book containing them.
(chiefly US) A distance that can be traveled in one hour.
d.e: This place is an hour away from where I live.

d.t: A structure built or serving as an abode of human beings.
d.e: This is my house and my family's ancestral home.

d.t: A container; a thing which houses another.
(uncountable) Size and quality of residential accommodations; housing.
A building intended to contain a single household, as opposed to an apartment or condominium or building containing these.
The people who live in a house; a household.
A building used for something other than a residence (typically with qualifying word).
d.e: The former carriage house had been made over into a guest house.

d.t: The audience for a live theatrical or similar performance.
d.e: After her swan-song, there wasn't a dry eye in the house.

d.t: (politics) A building where a deliberative assembly meets; whence the assembly itself, particularly a component of a legislature.
d.e: The petition was so ridiculous that the house rejected it after minimal debate.

d.t: A dynasty; a family with its ancestors and descendants, especially a royal or noble one.
d.e: A curse lay upon the House of Atreus.

d.t: (figurative) A place of rest or repose.
A grouping of schoolchildren for the purposes of competition in sports and other activities.
d.e: I was a member of Spenser house when I was at school.

d.t: An animal's shelter or den, or the shell of an animal such as a snail, used for protection.
(music) House music.
(transitive) To keep within a structure or container.
d.e: The car is housed in the garage.

d.t: (transitive) To admit to residence; to harbor.
To take shelter or lodging; to abide; to lodge.
(transitive, astrology) To dwell within one of the twelve astrological houses.
(transitive) To contain or cover mechanical parts.
(transitive) To contain one part of an object for the purpose of locating the whole.
d.e: The joists were housed into the side walls, rather than being hung from them.

d.t: (obsolete) To drive to a shelter.
(obsolete) To deposit and cover, as in the grave.
(nautical) To stow in a safe place; to take down and make safe.
d.e: to house the upper spars

d.t: (Canada, US, slang, transitive) To eat; especially, to scarf down.
d.e: All you wanna do is drink a fifth, house a lasagna, and hide in a dumpster until that baby stops crying.

d.t: (interrogative, degree) To what degree or extent.
d.e: How often do you practice?

d.t: (interrogative) In what manner:
(interrogative) In what state or condition.
d.e: How are you?

d.t: (fused relative) In the manner in which.
d.e: I said it exactly how he said it.

d.t: (fused relative) In any manner in which; in whatever way; however.
d.e: People should be free to live how they want.

d.t: (relative, nonstandard, modifying a word like way or manner) In which.
d.e: The way how you walk is funny.

d.t: (exclamative) Used as a modifier to indicate surprise, delight, or other strong feelings in an exclamation.
d.e: How very interesting!

d.t: (informal) Used to state that something is in a certain way or state.
d.e: She told me how her father was a doctor.

d.t: (US, dialectal) What?, pardon?
A greeting, used in representations of Native American speech.
The means by which something is accomplished.
d.e: I am not interested in the why, but in the how.

d.t: (dialectal) An artificial barrow or tumulus; in later folklore, associated with fairies.
(dialectal) In northern England, a low hill.
(not comparable) Of or belonging to the species Homo sapiens or its closest relatives.
(comparable) Having the nature or attributes of a human being.
d.e: To err is human; to forgive, divine.

d.t: Compassionate.
(strictly, biology) A highly intelligent ape with fine and short body hair; the most abundant species of primate, with members found on every continent (Homo sapiens).
d.e: Humans share common ancestors with other apes.

d.t: (loosely) Any hominid of the genus Homo.
(rare) To behave as or become, or to cause to behave as or become, a human.
A person; a large sapient, bipedal primate, with notably less hair than others of that order, of the species Homo sapiens.
Any member of the genus Homo, including extinct species.
(emphatic, ambitransitive) To hurry; to increase the speed of doing something.
